Setting aside the protection of ancient buildings, quarrying mountains for money is itself barbaric and short-sighted; if this is called economic development, then cutting flesh and selling eyes could also be called getting rich. I know ordinary people need food and clothing, need to marry and have children — an idle person like me shouldn't criticize, but I can't help feeling heartbroken! There seems to be a vicious cycle: the better the environment, the less developed the economy; to revitalize the economy, the only way is to destroy the environment. The so-called "living off the mountain" doesn't seem to mean this. Gazing at the distant river, ashamed of my inability to learn skills to benefit the people, I have little mood to repeat the information provided by Mr. Ma Yingjie: the Double Pagodas of Sanfu Temple are located in Zheli Village, Bailin Town, Fuding County. Sanfu Temple was built in the Song Dynasty; the double pagodas were first built in the Southern Song. According to the Qiu Family Genealogy, the existing pagodas were built in 1411 (the ninth year of Yongle reign, Ming). The current temple was rebuilt in modern times. The two pagodas are identical in form and size: brick pavilion-style, hexagonal, seven stories, 7.8 meters high. The body imitates timber structure, with columns at corners, four-puzuo bracket sets without shuatou; each story's roof is built up with corbelled courses, covered with cylindrical and flat tiles, with a gourd-shaped finial. During maintenance in 1986, many copper coins were unearthed from the finial, including Qin Banliang coins, Han Wuzhu coins, and Southern Song copper coins; also unearthed were silver standing figures inscribed with "donated by so-and-so," all indicating the pagoda was first built in the Song Dynasty.

projects.name: 仙蒲村
projects.address: 宁德福鼎县磻溪镇
projects.address_en: Panxi Town, Fuding County, Ningde
highlights: 村落格局
木结构
通体黑色建筑
望族合院住宅
林氏宗祠
古戏台
projects.content_zh: 从翠郊到仙蒲有30多公里的山路，都是新铺的水泥路，但有的路段比较狭窄，加上山路蜿蜒起伏，对自驾是个考验。不过游走于大山之中，周围人迹罕至，有如仙境一般。一路之上穿越了无数的竹林和茶园，这一地区盛产"福建白茶"，想起晚清人士李慈铭讽刺御史宝廷的诗句"曾因义女弹乌柏，妄逐京倡食白茶"，不禁笑出声来。当然，此白茶非彼白茶。终于到了，驻车于村口的河边，望着对岸成片的黑色大宅，确切的说是大寨子，难免有些发愣。正发愁附近静得出奇，想找个人打听一下，不想竟有人敲车窗：师傅您今天回去吗，能不能带我出去？仙蒲在山的那一边，信步走过石桥，穿过那条称作"仙蒲溪"的大溪，进入了那些黑色大型建筑错落的仙蒲村。大屋鳞次栉比，规模大小参差，静卧于山水田地之间。屋宇之间相隔不远，又保有独立的空间，一派和谐景象。给人印象最深的，除建筑的精巧外，就是通体的黑色，与周围满山的绿色形成鲜明的令人愉悦的反差。现存有清代以来的古民居数十座，保存完好的依次有外泮林氏民居、外头林氏民居、中头林氏民居、内头林氏民居、桥头林氏民居、大厝里林氏民居、花门楼林氏民居，另外还有林氏宗祠。仙蒲民居建筑典型者为望族合院住宅，两侧厢房对称布置。结构式样基本采用重檐歇山顶，穿斗式木构架。民居两侧均有阁楼式翘檐，面阔多在8至11间，进深7至12柱之间，规模不小。独自在村中穿行游荡，偶尔有热情的大姐介绍去参观某某院落。民居庭前都设四角庭院，大门进入后是条石夹锭的通道，直到前面的大厅。通道砌石阶二至三级，以青石打造的石鼓分布通道两侧。庭院坪铺以青石子，光亮而整洁；有的是夯平泥地，平实而整饬。四周以条石为框架，落落大方。厅堂是古民居最为精心装点之处，木雕装饰繁多。古祠、古庙、古井构成村落三大元素。村落中心处的林氏宗祠为清代建筑，祠堂前立有棋杆夹，铺以青石坪，场地开阔。祠内古戏台、天井及藻井手绘人物故事。宗祠的形制代表着外来的中原文化，是我们一眼能够辨识得出的，又似乎与当地的特色建筑关系不大。就要离开了，来时想要搭车的年轻人小林过来，听说我是来探访古村的，又热情地拉我去多看几处，他们家就住在一处很大的古宅中，不过是在河的这一边。由于对当地的建筑风格和文化源流心存疑惑，我特意问他祖上是汉族的还是畲族？他很确切地说是汉族，"祖上是从中原举家迁来的"。回去的路上有小林做伴就不寂寞了。到了附近的镇上，小林还执意请我去吃当地的一家面馆，"很有名气的，来了总归要尝一尝"，虽然门面有些简陋，但味道确实好，食客都是当地人。小林还特意请来自己的小学老师，着实令人感动。仙蒲不负其名，乃喜欢摄影和古建筑的朋友不可错过之地，当然同行之人中最好再有一喜欢自驾的挑战一战。如果你是三种爱好集大成者，那就独自前往领略一下那一路的气息，毕竟很多东西只有独自品味方能体会其中的妙处。
projects.content_en: From Cuijiao to Xianpu is over 30 kilometers of mountain road, all newly paved concrete, but some sections are narrow, and with the winding, undulating mountain road, it is a test for self-driving. Yet wandering in the great mountains, with few people around, feels like a fairyland. Along the way, one passes through countless bamboo groves and tea gardens — this region produces "Fujian White Tea." Recalling the late Qing poem by Li Ciming mocking censor Bao Ting — "Once denounced a righteous daughter for the tallow tree, recklessly followed Beijing courtesans eating white tea" — I couldn't help laughing. Of course, this white tea is not that white tea. Finally arriving, I parked by the river at the village entrance, gazing at the clusters of black grand mansions across the river — or rather, large stockaded villages — and couldn't help being stunned. Worrying that it was eerily quiet nearby and wanting to ask someone, unexpectedly someone knocked on the car window: "Master, are you going back today? Can you take me out?" Xianpu is on the other side of the mountain. Walking across the stone bridge, crossing the wide stream called "Xianpu Stream," I entered Xianpu Village with its scattered large black buildings. The grand houses stand in rows, varying in size, quietly nestled among mountains, waters, and fields. The buildings are not far apart yet retain independent space — a scene of harmony. What impresses most, besides the exquisite architecture, is the uniform black color, forming a striking and pleasant contrast with the surrounding green mountains. Dozens of ancient residences from the Qing onward survive; well-preserved ones include the Waipan Lin Residence, Waitou Lin Residence, Zhongtou Lin Residence, Neitou Lin Residence, Qiaotou Lin Residence, Dacuo Li Lin Residence, and Hualoumen Lin Residence, plus the Lin Ancestral Hall. Typical Xianpu residences are wealthy clan courtyard houses with symmetrically placed side wings. The structural form basically uses double-eave hip-and-gable roofs with column-and-tie timber frames. Both sides of residences have attic-style upturned eaves, with widths mostly 8-11 bays and depths 7-12 columns — not small in scale. Wandering alone through the village, occasionally an enthusiastic woman would introduce me to visit a certain courtyard. Residences have four-corner courtyards in front; entering the gate, a channel of dressed stone slabs leads to the front hall. The channel has 2-3 stone steps, with blue-stone drum stones on both sides. The courtyard is paved with blue pebbles, bright and tidy; some are tamped earth, plain and neat. Dressed stone frames surround all sides, graceful and大方. The hall is the most elaborately decorated part of ancient residences, with numerous wood carvings. Ancient ancestral halls, temples, and wells form the three major elements of the village. The Lin Ancestral Hall at the village center is a Qing building, with flagpole clamps in front and a blue-stone paved courtyard, spacious. Inside, the ancient stage, courtyard, and caisson ceiling have hand-painted human stories. The ancestral hall's form represents imported Central Plains culture — recognizable at a glance, yet seemingly unrelated to local characteristic architecture. About to leave, the young man Xiao Lin who wanted a ride came over; hearing I was visiting ancient villages, he enthusiastically took me to see more places. His family lives in a large ancient house, on this side of the river. Wondering about the local architectural style and cultural origins, I specifically asked whether his ancestors were Han or She ethnicity. He firmly said Han: "My ancestors moved the whole family here from the Central Plains." On the way back, with Xiao Lin as company, I was not lonely. In the nearby town, Xiao Lin insisted on treating me to a local noodle shop — "It's famous, you must try it when you come." Though the storefront was simple, the taste was indeed good, and customers were all locals. Xiao Lin even specially invited his elementary school teacher, truly moving. Xianpu lives up to its name — a must-visit for photography and ancient architecture enthusiasts; of course, it's best to have a companion who enjoys self-driving challenges. If you are a master of all three passions, then go alone to savor the atmosphere of the journey — after all, many things can only be fully appreciated when tasted alone.

projects.name: 昭明寺
projects.address: 宁德市福鼎县桐山镇柯岭村
projects.address_en: Keling Village, Tongshan Town, Fuding County, Ningde
highlights: 早期遗址
历代更改痕迹
南朝梁大通元年建
昭明太子萧统所建
六角砖塔昭明寺塔
释迦牟尼佛舍利
projects.content_zh: 古刹南朝地，登临远世尘。鸟啼山外树，人踏岭头云。塔影参天留，钟声带雁闻。兴亡思帝子，黄叶落纷纷。昭明寺位于福建省福鼎县城西3.5公里的鳌峰山顶，建于南朝梁大通元年（527年），距今已近一千五百年历史。相传为昭明太子萧统所建，故名。明嘉靖十三年（1534年）重修。寺内现有山门、天王殿、大雄宝殿、钟楼、法堂、禅堂、藏经楼、净土堂、玉佛楼、白衣阁和六角砖塔等。寺内供有释迦牟尼佛舍利一粒，迎自斯里兰卡，为镇寺之宝。昭明寺建筑的一大亮点是位于寺内的六角砖塔昭明寺塔。该塔塔基面积47平方米，塔身高25.6米，六角七层，为楼阁式仿木结构空心砖塔。塔外观与当地白琳镇的双福寺双塔有些相像，虽工艺不及双塔繁复，但体量要大得多。塔内有扶梯，登塔顶可鸟瞰桐城全景，每当傍晚时分，昭明寺塔与夕阳交相辉映，相伴阵阵低沉的梵钟，此景称为"昭明夕照"。说到当地人，他们似乎偏爱粉色，乡间的妇女们的传统服装就是通身粉色，很多建筑包括坟茔也都饰以粉色，昭明寺塔也不例外。开始有些不解，当在此盛开的杜鹃花下仰望巨塔，似乎突然明白，那是象征旺盛生命力之美的颜色。昭明寺的佛事很盛，寺内香火旺盛，诵经之声相闻，善男信女多有前来，还有人来掣签祈福，是当地不可多得的佛教圣地。
projects.content_en: An ancient temple of the Southern Dynasties, climbing it distances one from the world. Birds sing in trees beyond the mountain, people tread clouds at the ridge top. The pagoda shadow reaches the sky, the bell sound carries with wild geese. Thinking of the prince in rise and fall, yellow leaves fall in profusion. Zhaoming Temple sits atop Aofeng Mountain, 3.5 kilometers west of Fuding County seat, Fujian. Built in 527 (the first year of Datong reign, Southern Dynasties Liang), it has a history of nearly 1,500 years. According to legend, it was built by Crown Prince Zhaoming (Xiao Tong), hence the name. Restored in 1534 (the 13th year of Jiajing reign, Ming). The temple now has a gate, Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, bell tower, Dharma hall, meditation hall, scripture library, Pure Land hall, Jade Buddha building, White Robe pavilion, and a hexagonal brick pagoda. The temple houses one relic of Shakyamuni Buddha, brought from Sri Lanka, as its treasure. A major highlight of Zhaoming Temple's architecture is the hexagonal brick pagoda inside. The pagoda base covers 47 square meters, the body is 25.6 meters high, hexagonal with seven stories, a pavilion-style imitation-timber hollow brick pagoda. Its appearance resembles the Double Pagodas of Shuangfu Temple in local Bailin Town; though less intricate in craftsmanship, it is much larger in scale. Inside the pagoda is a staircase; climbing to the top offers a panoramic view of Tongcheng. At dusk, the Zhaoming Temple Pagoda glows with the setting sun, accompanied by the deep sound of the Buddhist bell — this scene is called "Zhaoming Evening Glow." Speaking of locals, they seem to favor pink: rural women's traditional clothing is entirely pink, and many buildings including tombs are decorated in pink — Zhaoming Temple Pagoda is no exception. At first puzzled, looking up at the giant pagoda under blooming azaleas, I suddenly understood: it is the color symbolizing the beauty of vigorous life. Zhaoming Temple's Buddhist activities are thriving, with abundant incense and the sound of chanting; many devotees come, and some draw lots for blessings — a rare Buddhist holy place locally.

projects.name: 半月里古村
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德霞浦县溪南镇
projects.address_en: Xinan Town, Xiapu County, Ningde
highlights: 村落格局
木结构
石作做法
畲族历史文化名村
龙溪宫
雷世儒大厝
projects.content_zh: 半月里，曾名"半路里"是畲族聚居的村庄。村庄东望玉兔山，与白露坑村有一山之隔，背靠状如弯月的弥勒山山麓，南临双福桥水库。半月里被誉为"畲族历史文化名村"，有近300年历史的龙溪宫（省级文物保护单位）、雷世儒大厝、雷位进故居、雷志茂故居、秀才院、雷氏宗祠（均被省政府列入文物保护单位龙溪宫的附属保护单位）。龙溪宫始建清雍正八年（1730年），背靠弥勒山，面向玉兔山、东依燕鼎山，建筑面积508平方米，硬山顶抬梁、穿斗木结构，由斗、升、翘、昂、拱组合。自南而北依次为大门、戏台、众厅、神厅、神龛等。其戏台藻井以五层方斗逐级装嵌，形成远观四方、近视八角的藻井。宫中供奉有畲民信仰的神祇薛元帅（唐代大将薛仁贵）、陈元帅（唐五代武将陈九郎亦称九仙）、平水明王（杨从仪，宋朝大将，治水功臣）和雷万春元帅（唐代大将）等神祇。雷世儒，清朝武举人，他武艺高强又善于经商，积累了雄厚的资金。道光年间建大厝，大小房间38间，柱子126根，占地1300平方米。古宅雕梁画栋，气势非凡，且存文物颇丰。是闽东地区重要的畲族文物古迹。雷位进故居也颇耐看，门楼不显而厅堂敞亮。正屋位于最高处，虽然有些破败，依旧能看出当年气派。屋檐双层，确实极具特色。村中一片静谧，大量的使用石料，坚固与美观兼备，也成了整个村落的建筑基调。我们听到的唯一人声是几个妇女在拉家常，走过去一看，是一位大姐和两个身着传统民族服装的老奶奶在门边交谈。我们上前打招呼问路，老奶奶很和善微笑，但语言不通。大姐非常热情给我们指路，后来又不放心亲自追过来把该走的一道不起眼的门指给我们才走了，与人为善以至于此，当地民风可见。半月里古村的生活像古树，祥和，无言，老了。我们这群年轻人，陪伴老人的时间不多，总是有路要赶。尽管尚有比较重要的古迹没有看完，那份安详也是令人留恋，不过世事无全，看见就是缘分，略有缺憾，留待下次造访。
projects.content_en: Banyueli, formerly called "Banluli," is a She ethnic minority village. The village faces Yutu Mountain to the east, separated from Bailukeng Village by one mountain, backed by the foot of Mile Mountain shaped like a crescent moon, and south of Shuangfuqiao Reservoir. Banyueli is hailed as a "She Ethnic Historical and Cultural Village," with the nearly 300-year-old Longxi Palace (provincial cultural heritage site), Lei Shiru's Grand Mansion, Lei Weijin's Former Residence, Lei Zhimao's Former Residence, Xiucai Courtyard, and Lei Ancestral Hall (all listed by the provincial government as affiliated protection units of Longxi Palace). Longxi Palace was founded in 1730 (the eighth year of Yongzheng reign, Qing), backed by Mile Mountain, facing Yutu Mountain, and east of Yanding Mountain, with a building area of 508 square meters. It has a gable roof with beam-lifting and column-and-tie timber structure, composed of dou (blocks), sheng (blocks), qiao (arms), ang (levers), and gong (arms). From south to north, it consists of the gate, stage, assembly hall, deity hall, and shrine. The stage's caisson ceiling is assembled with five layers of square blocks, forming a ceiling that looks square from afar and octagonal up close. The palace worships deities believed in by the She people: Marshal Xue (Tang general Xue Rengui), Marshal Chen (Five Dynasties general Chen Jiulang, also called Jiuxian), Pingshui Mingwang (Yang Congyi, Song general and flood-control hero), and Marshal Lei Wanchun (Tang general). Lei Shiru, a Qing military juren, was highly skilled in martial arts and adept at business, accumulating substantial wealth. During the Daoguang reign, he built a grand mansion with 38 rooms of various sizes, 126 columns, covering 1,300 square meters. The ancient mansion has carved beams and painted rafters, extraordinary presence, and abundant relics — an important She ethnic cultural relic in eastern Fujian. Lei Weijin's Former Residence is also worth seeing: the gate is unassuming but the hall is bright. The main house sits at the highest point; though somewhat dilapidated, its former grandeur is still visible. The double eaves are truly distinctive. The village is serene, with extensive use of stone — both sturdy and beautiful — forming the architectural基调 of the entire village. The only human voices we heard were several women chatting; approaching, we saw a middle-aged woman and two grandmothers in traditional ethnic clothing talking by the door. We greeted and asked for directions; the grandmothers smiled kindly but we couldn't communicate. The middle-aged woman enthusiastically showed us the way, then, worried, personally chased after us to point out an inconspicuous door we should take before leaving — such kindness reveals the local character. Life in Banyueli Ancient Village is like an old tree: peaceful, wordless, aged. We young people have little time to accompany the elderly, always having roads to travel. Though some important relics remain unseen, that tranquility is unforgettable; but nothing is perfect in this world — seeing is fate, with slight shortcomings left for the next visit.

projects.name: 传胪城堡
projects.address: 宁德霞浦县传胪村
projects.address_en: Chuanlu Village, Xiapu County, Ningde
highlights: 城堡堡墙
砖石结构
明嘉靖年间抗倭筑堡
地中海风格小镇
废弃歌剧院
projects.content_zh: 传胪城堡位于霞浦县南部半岛地区，西邻海湾，一路空气清新，风光明丽。传胪城堡建于明嘉靖年间，据《霞浦县志〈大事记〉》载："明嘉靖年间连年倭寇侵犯东南各乡，以戚参将奏准沿海各乡筑堡，墙上遍植岩柴树自卫……于是乡人始知有城堡之利，而沿海五十七堡，次第筑云。"而名曰"传胪"，想必是因为当地出过全国科举考试第四而得名。该堡周长640米，呈正方形，城内占地面积2009平方米，城堡部分已残破，高约4米，座基宽5米，墙顶宽3.5米，为花岗岩碎石干砌。原建城辟有西、南、北三处城门，南门于1988年重修，城门高5米，呈圆形，门内外圆内方，城门内宽2.5米，内高4米，城门眉顶嵌刻黑底金字"皇明方伯里"碑刻。西城门因濒于倒塌，2003年民材自筹拆建，形成圆形城门，城门内宽2.4米，内高3.2米。三处城门均为块石砌体，城墙就地取材为碎石或鹅卵石干砌。而在城墙遍植岩柴树，原为260余株，由于多次受飓风摧毁，现仅存200多株，根深蒂固地盘错在石墙上。城堡内的民居大多为这种半月形门，村中原有民居统一是斜坡顶的建筑，整体看去俨然一地中海风格的小镇，风格非常独特。堡内有废弃的歌剧院，内部双层看台，保存仍旧完好。带有西洋风格的建筑在堡内随处可见。
projects.content_en: Chuanlu Castle is located in the southern peninsula region of Xiapu County, west of the bay, with fresh air and bright scenery along the way. Chuanlu Castle was built during the Jiajing reign of the Ming. According to the "Major Events" section of Xiapu County Gazetteer: "During the Jiajing reign of the Ming, Japanese pirates repeatedly invaded southeastern villages; upon General Qi's memorial approval, coastal villages built fortresses, with rock-brier trees planted all over the walls for self-defense... Thus villagers came to know the benefits of castles, and the 57 coastal fortresses were built one after another." The name "Chuanlu" (Fourth Place in Imperial Exam) presumably comes from a local who placed fourth in the national imperial examination. The castle has a perimeter of 640 meters, square in plan, with an interior area of 2,009 square meters. Part of the castle is dilapidated, about 4 meters high, with a base width of 5 meters and top width of 3.5 meters, built of dry-laid granite rubble. Originally it had three city gates — west, south, and north. The south gate was restored in 1988: 5 meters high, circular, round outside and square inside, 2.5 meters wide and 4 meters high inside, with a black-background gold-character inscription "Huangming Fangbeli" embedded above the gate. The west gate, near collapse, was demolished and rebuilt by villagers in 2003, forming a circular gate 2.4 meters wide and 3.2 meters high inside. All three gates are built of dressed stone; the walls use local rubble or cobblestones dry-laid. Rock-brier trees were planted all over the walls — originally over 260, now only over 200 survive after repeated hurricane destruction, their roots deeply intertwined in the stone walls. Most residences inside the castle have these crescent-shaped doors; the original residences uniformly had sloped roofs, making the whole village look like a Mediterranean-style town, very unique in style. Inside the castle is an abandoned opera house with double-tiered seating, still well preserved. Western-style buildings can be seen everywhere inside the castle.

projects.name: 大京城堡
projects.address: 宁德霞浦县大京村
projects.address_en: Dajing Village, Xiapu County, Ningde
highlights: 城堡堡墙
城堡格局
明洪武20年海防巡检司千户所
海涯屏藩
瓮城双重城
projects.content_zh: 大京城堡也在霞浦县南部半岛地区，东临大海。远眺海上仙山，俯瞰大京可辨。明朝初年，明太祖为抗御倭寇的侵扰，于明洪武20年（公元1387年）下诏设海防巡检司千户所（福宁卫大金守御千户所），在确定处所时，大京被选中并列名12千户所首位，江夏侯周德兴执行朱元璋"高筑墙"战略，在这里兴建城堡，规模远比其他千户所为大。城周长2815米，高6.5至9米不等，墙面宽3.6米，座基宽5.6米，系花岗岩砌成，辟东、西、南三门（北面依山），东门为瓮城，也叫双重城，砌石缝均以铁水浇固。城上有数百个垛口，俯瞰远眺，视野十分壮阔，情境一览无遗。城外有一条宽宽的护城河，与城堡构成一个森严壁垒的整体。城上窝铺、炮位等设备齐全，与外海烽火门、南日山互为表里，结为犄角，形成坚固的防御体系，阻遏了海上盗寇的觊觎骚扰、人称"海涯屏藩"。城内一条以条石拼铺的宽7米的大街直贯东西，长1200米，并按一定距离兴建迎恩等4个街亭，开凿4口八角大井。现如今城堡内大多是古民居，百年甚至几百年老屋鳞次栉比。堡内与传胪样式相同带有拱形大门的民居也是随处可见。渔村的特殊景致。少时经常看小人书《丁丁历险记》，里面那个可爱的船长经常咒骂"该死的成千上万只贝壳壳"，眼前就是原物了。
projects.content_en: Dajing Castle is also in the southern peninsula region of Xiapu County, facing the sea to the east. Looking far at the immortal mountains at sea, one can discern Dajing below. In the early Ming, to resist Japanese pirate incursions, the Hongwu Emperor issued an edict in 1387 (the 20th year of Hongwu reign) to establish coastal defense inspection offices and thousand-household garrisons (the Funing Guard Dajing Defense Thousand-Household Garrison). When selecting the site, Dajing was chosen and ranked first among 12 thousand-household garrisons. Zhou Dexing, Marquis of Jiangxia, executing Zhu Yuanzhang's "build high walls" strategy, constructed a castle here, much larger than other thousand-household garrisons. The city wall has a perimeter of 2,815 meters, height varying from 6.5 to 9 meters, wall surface 3.6 meters wide, base 5.6 meters wide, built of granite, with three gates — east, west, and south (the north leans on the mountain). The east gate is a barbican, also called a double city, with stone joints all reinforced with poured iron. There are hundreds of crenellations on the wall; overlooking from above, the view is magnificent and the scene fully visible. Outside the city runs a wide moat, forming an impregnable whole with the castle. Barracks, artillery positions, and other facilities are complete on the wall; together with the Fenghuo Gate and Nanri Mountain at sea, they form a solid defensive system, deterring sea pirates — called the "Seaside Barrier." Inside the city, a 7-meter-wide street paved with dressed stones runs straight east-west, 1,200 meters long, with four street pavilions including Ying'en built at intervals, and four large octagonal wells dug. Today, most buildings inside the castle are ancient residences, with century-old or even multi-century-old houses standing in rows. Residences with arched gates in the same style as Chuanlu can be seen everywhere inside. The special scenery of a fishing village. As a child I often read the comic "The Adventures of Tintin," in which the lovable captain constantly cursed "damn thousands upon thousands of seashells" — here before my eyes is the original.

projects.name: 观音亭寨
projects.address: 宁德霞浦县水门畲族乡半岭村
projects.address_en: Banling Village, Shuimen She Ethnic Township, Xiapu County, Ningde
highlights: 寨堡堡墙
寨门石作
明洪武二年建
畲族盘诗对歌
16块碑刻
projects.content_zh: 观音亭寨遗址位于福建省霞浦县水门畲族乡半岭村东300米。观音亭寨所在的半岭村附近有大片的茶叶种植园。村子始建于明洪武二年（1369年），清康熙五年重建，清同治二年扩建。寨堡依山势，沿东北方向筑寨墙，用条石和乱毛石砌筑。残墙尚存118米长，高5.4米。只设东寨门，门楣石刻楷书"观音亭寨"4字。亭门外，竖有16块碑刻。清代福宁总兵曾派士兵在此驻守。观音寨内原有观音寺，现重修一新，后面有8个畲族村落。每当正月十五元宵佳节，闽浙当地畲族民众依照数百年旧俗来此聚集，进行祭祀以外，尚有盘诗、对歌等庆祝活动。说实在观音亭遗址作为古建筑存留的不是很多，给人留下更多印象的是一路寻来那份曲径通幽的妙趣，保存完好的自然环境和大日长空之下空无一人的震撼。将要离开时路过观音寺，遇到一老尼，问我从哪里来，并告诉我上面还有可以游观之处，遂跟着她穿方丈而过，拾阶而上就见到上面的古树，着实赞叹了一番。再往上走是一规模较小的供奉观音的所在。正当此时接到夫人来电，诉说面临早产之忧的小嫂正在医院的观察室焦灼等待。余无能为力之下只能宽慰数语。谁知3小时后告知顺产双胞胎男婴，母子平安，高兴之余感叹此观音如此慈悲。
projects.content_en: The Guanyinting Stockade site is located 300 meters east of Banling Village, Shuimen She Ethnic Township, Xiapu County, Fujian. Near Banling Village where Guanyinting Stockade sits are large tea plantations. The village was founded in 1369 (the second year of Hongwu reign, Ming), rebuilt in the fifth year of Kangxi reign (Qing), and expanded in the second year of Tongzhi reign (Qing). The stockade follows the terrain, with walls built along the northeast direction using dressed stones and rough stones. The remaining wall is 118 meters long and 5.4 meters high. Only the east stockade gate exists, with the stone lintel carved in regular script "Guanyinting Zhai" (Guanyin Pavilion Stockade). Outside the pavilion gate stand 16 steles. During the Qing, the Funing garrison commander stationed soldiers here. Inside Guanyin Stockade was originally Guanyin Temple, now newly restored, with 8 She ethnic villages behind it. Every year on the 15th day of the first lunar month (Lantern Festival), local She people from Fujian and Zhejiang gather here according to centuries-old customs, conducting sacrifices plus antiphonal singing and other celebrations. Honestly, not much of Guanyinting site survives as ancient architecture; what leaves more impression is the charm of winding paths leading to seclusion along the way, the well-preserved natural environment, and the震撼 of being completely alone under the vast sky. About to leave, I passed Guanyin Temple and met an old nun who asked where I came from and told me there were more places to see above. Following her through the abbot's quarters and up the steps, I saw ancient trees above and was truly amazed. Further up was a smaller place enshrining Guanyin. Just then I received a call from my wife, saying my sister-in-law, facing premature labor, was anxiously waiting in the hospital's observation room. Helpless, I could only offer a few words of comfort. Who knew that three hours later I was told she had safely delivered twin boys, mother and children well — in my joy I sighed that this Guanyin is so compassionate.

projects.name: 上村
projects.address: 宁德霞浦县盐田畲族乡
projects.address_en: Yantian She Ethnic Township, Xiapu County, Ningde
highlights: 村落格局
木结构
石作做法
霞浦县唯一古村落
清中期古宅
严丝合缝杉木作
projects.content_zh: 上村位于霞浦县西，偏北，驾车行约30余公里可至。虽然不是国家命名的历史文化名村，却在福建博物院编辑出版的《福建北部古村落调查报告》中作为霞浦县唯一的古村落榜上有名，我们自然怀着好奇的心态前去一探究竟。上村坐落于青山绿水之间，沿着一条大溪深入，就是通向上村的路。如果使用电子地图要搜索"毕厝里"，再向北一点手动寻找"上村"，否则容易与别的"上村"搞混。上村所在地区也是畲族聚居区，沿途青山环抱，旁边河水流过，这样的风水上佳之地很早就有人居住了。相对于来自中原地区的客家人，畲族属于早期定居于此的，开始从事渔猎活动，信奉萨满教，完全定居后受中原文化影响较大，村落中也注重营造庙宇、祠堂等建筑。快到上村的时候看到比较大的古宅。古宅的一面看上去比较气派，可以想见当年风采，另一面堆满柴草，充满生活气息。站在村后的高地眺望，整个村落尽收眼底，感叹上村的先民选址的精当。整个村落就那么静静地安卧于此，没有一点声音，又仿佛诉说了很多。这里有纯朴热情的人们，有清新典雅、古意盎然的建筑，那种气质似乎比完全的农人多了几分雅致，比完全的读书人多了几分洒脱，比完全的商人多了几分自然，也许这是畲族人祖传的特有气质。巧遇古宅的主人罗先生，见我们在外面拍摄，热情地邀请我们进到里面参观，并做了详细介绍。这所古宅建于清中期，距今已有200多年，宅子的规模不是很大，但设计精巧，足见当初的主人不但家境殷实，而且在细节处也用了不少心思。本来这一带汤姓是大姓，罗先生自我介绍属于后来住进此宅的贫下中农，但现在已经拥有宅子的产权，一家人祖孙三代安居于此。宅院中寂静无人，只有地面上淡淡的青苔。宅子在那里，静静地敞开着，没有人阻止，也没有人欢迎，只有脚踩在地面上发出的轻微的声响。偶尔有飞鸟从宅院上空的头顶飞过，扑扇翅膀的声音清晰可闻。宅子里面的木工活儿非常讲究，选材是上好的杉木，虽不见繁复的雕饰，但衔接处严丝合缝，历经长久岁月，也未加特意的保养，居然没有任何变形，摸上去光滑如新，令人惊叹。宅内有供女人梳头的长椅，对镜一瞥，内外旖旎风光。看不出罗先生已经61岁了，据他说日常还在经营农活儿，农闲时也去工厂打工，加工海带。"自己做活自己吃一点。"这里的生活非常安逸，夏天很凉快，也没有拥挤和噪音。我们羡慕他算是半个神仙了，他很高兴，还要留我们吃饭。祝愿他合家平安幸福！
projects.content_en: Shangcun Village is located west of Xiapu County, slightly north, about 30 kilometers by car. Though not a nationally designated historical and cultural village, it is listed as the only ancient village in Xiapu County in the "Investigation Report on Ancient Villages of Northern Fujian" published by the Fujian Museum — naturally we went to explore with curiosity. Shangcun sits among green mountains and clear waters; following a large stream deep in leads to the road to Shangcun. If using electronic maps, search "Bicuoli," then manually find "Shangcun" a bit north, otherwise it's easy to confuse with other "Shangcun" villages. The area around Shangcun is also a She ethnic settlement; along the way, green mountains embrace and a river flows beside — such excellent fengshui land was inhabited early. Compared with Hakka people from the Central Plains, the She are earlier settlers here, initially engaged in fishing and hunting, believing in shamanism; after fully settling, they were greatly influenced by Central Plains culture, and villages also emphasize building temples and ancestral halls. Nearing Shangcun, we saw a relatively large ancient house. One side of the house looks imposing, evoking its former glory; the other side is piled with firewood, full of life. Standing on high ground behind the village, the whole village comes into view, and one sighs at the wisdom of Shangcun's ancestors in choosing the site. The whole village lies quietly here, without a sound, yet as if telling much. Here are simple and warm people, fresh and elegant, ancient-tinged buildings — that temperament seems a bit more refined than pure farmers, a bit more free-spirited than pure scholars, a bit more natural than pure merchants — perhaps this is the inherited characteristic temperament of the She people. We happened to meet the owner of the ancient house, Mr. Luo, who, seeing us photographing outside, warmly invited us in for a visit and gave a detailed introduction. This ancient house was built in the mid-Qing, over 200 years ago. The house is not very large but exquisitely designed, showing that the original owner was not only well-off but also paid much attention to details. Originally the Tang surname was dominant in this area; Mr. Luo introduced himself as a poor peasant who later moved into the house, but now owns the property, with three generations of his family living here. The courtyard is silent and empty, with only faint moss on the ground. The house stands there, quietly open, with no one stopping or welcoming — only the slight sound of feet on the ground. Occasionally a bird flies overhead across the courtyard, the sound of flapping wings clearly audible. The woodwork inside the house is very refined, using excellent Chinese fir; though no complex carvings, the joints are perfectly tight. After long years without special maintenance, there is surprisingly no deformation, and it feels smooth as new — amazing. Inside the house is a long bench for women to comb their hair; a glance in the mirror reveals charming scenery inside and out. Mr. Luo doesn't look 61; he says he still does farm work daily, and in slack seasons works in a factory processing kelp. "Work myself, eat a little myself." Life here is very comfortable, cool in summer, without crowding or noise. We envied him as half an immortal; he was delighted and even wanted to keep us for dinner. Wishing his family peace and happiness!

projects.name: 大宝桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县坑底乡小东村
projects.address_en: Xiaodong Village, Kengdi Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
长44米拱跨32米
projects.content_zh: 大宝桥位于寿宁县坑底乡小东村水尾，因此又称小东下桥，始建于明代，清光绪年间重修。大宝桥静卧于小村之中，外观端庄，顶部线条较直，略加装饰，风雨板全封闭。桥体量巨大，长44米，拱跨32米，这样的大桥似乎本应凌驾于高山险壑之中，与其下面这条潺潺流过的小溪殊不相称。也许是寿宁境内的廊桥宗匠们在卖弄技艺？造桥工艺的规整堪称典范，用材也不一般，三节苗所取大木长度很长，把桥身高高架起。廊屋四柱九檩抬梁式木架构，19间，80柱，地面的。
projects.content_en: Dabao Bridge is located at the water's end of Xiaodong Village, Kengdi Township, Shouning County, hence also called Xiaodong Lower Bridge. Founded in the Ming Dynasty, it was restored during the Guangxu reign of the Qing. Dabao Bridge lies quietly in the small village, with a dignified appearance, relatively straight top lines, slight decoration, and fully enclosed wind-and-rain boards. The bridge is massive, 44 meters long with an arch span of 32 meters — such a large bridge should seemingly span high mountains and deep ravines, quite mismatched with the gurgling stream below. Perhaps the covered-bridge masters of Shouning were showing off their skills? The bridge-building craftsmanship is exemplary in regularity, and the materials are extraordinary: the large timbers used for the three-section miao are very long, raising the bridge body high. The covered hall has a four-column nine-purlin beam-lifting timber frame, 19 bays and 80 columns.

projects.name: 福寿桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县犀溪乡西浦村
projects.address_en: Xipu Village, Xixi Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
状元树
三节苗用材很长
projects.content_zh: 福寿桥所在的寿宁县犀溪乡西浦村，村口有参天古树，名曰状元树，因为村里宋代出过状元。未见木桥，先见石桥跨于大溪之上，名曰永安桥。西浦村延溪而建，而村中小巷内又有小溪流过。村中小巷深深，小门寂寂；村中乐队在老者的带领下正在认真地排练古老的乐曲，大概是祭祖时要演奏的，巨大的水车缓缓转动，连接着古古道。过河出现一段保存尚好的古道。古道是寿宁通往泰顺的古商道，眼下将我们引向福寿桥。福寿桥也算得大桥了，三节苗用材很长，桥面隆起很高，桥墩建的十分规整。廊屋内祀观音、玄武大帝和临水夫人，匾额虽新但字体潇洒遒劲。廊屋梁柱上所见题记不多。不知道为什么离开西浦村这块曾经风景如画而且明摆着的人文荟萃之地，笔者非但没有什么恋恋不舍，反而有种逃离之感。原本我们的任务虽不是歌功颂德，但也没必要恶语中伤，只是西浦太具有代表性，代表着自古以来就是人文和商业旺地，眼下也是明显富裕起来的中国的乡村。其实村中的那些古建筑都是笔者费尽心思从钢筋水泥的丛林中挑拣出来的，而且绝大多数古宅都已经破败不堪，无人居住了。经济的大潮无法阻挡，因为它代表着人们追求美好生活的愿望，这种动力无疑是强大的。但看着一边虽然破败，但明显曾经美轮美奂并且与自然环境相得益彰的古老村落，一边看着张牙舞爪、毫无美感和建筑规划可言的现代民居，笔者真的怀疑我们是当初中国人的子孙吗？我们和曾经创造这一文明和审美模式。
projects.content_en: Xipu Village in Xixi Township, Shouning County, where Fushou Bridge stands, has a towering ancient tree at the village entrance called the Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Tree, because the village produced a top scholar in the Song Dynasty. Before seeing the timber bridge, one first sees a stone bridge spanning the large stream, called Yong'an Bridge. Xipu Village was built along the stream, and small streams also flow through the village alleys. The village alleys are deep, the small doors silent; a village band under the leadership of an elder is earnestly rehearsing ancient music, probably to be played during ancestor worship. A huge water wheel slowly turns, connecting ancient paths. Crossing the river, a well-preserved section of ancient path appears. This ancient path was the trade route from Shouning to Taishun, now leading us to Fushou Bridge. Fushou Bridge can also be considered a large bridge: the three-section miao uses very long timbers, the deck rises high, and the piers are built very regularly. Inside the covered hall are enshrined Guanyin, the Xuanwu Great Emperor, and the Waterside Lady; though the plaques are new, the calligraphy is free and powerful. Few inscriptions are seen on the beams and columns of the covered hall. I don't know why, leaving Xipu Village — this once picturesque and obviously culturally rich place — I felt not reluctance but rather a sense of escape. Our task is not to sing praises, but there's no need for malicious criticism either; it's just that Xipu is too representative, representing a place that has been a cultural and commercial hub since ancient times, and now an obviously prosperous Chinese village. In fact, those ancient buildings in the village were ones I painstakingly picked out from the jungle of reinforced concrete, and the vast majority of ancient mansions are already dilapidated and uninhabited. The tide of economy cannot be stopped, because it represents people's desire for a better life, and this drive is undoubtedly powerful. But looking at one side — though dilapidated, clearly once magnificent and harmonizing with the natural environment — and the other side — modern residences that are aggressive, without aesthetic sense or architectural planning — I truly doubt whether we are the descendants of the original Chinese? We and those who once created this civilization and aesthetic model.

projects.name: 观音桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县凤阳乡大石村
projects.address_en: Dashi Village, Fengyang Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
八字支撑结构
三重檐桥屋
清道光二十年建成
projects.content_zh: 很奇怪，在福建北部寿宁县与周宁县交界处，寿宁县有一个楔形区域深入周宁县境内，不知辖区如此划分有何奥妙，总之在周宁去往寿宁县的路上不小心已经进入寿宁境内，不知不觉又出来了。在这一区域路边，偶然发现了一座藏在深山、鲜为人知的八字撑木廊桥，本以为是在周宁境内，后来才知道这是我们进入廊桥之乡寿宁县有幸见到的第一座廊桥。看上去此桥与周宁县境内纯池镇的几座廊桥如三仙桥、七仙桥、院林桥非常相似。整个桥体结构合理，比例匀称，保护完好，与青山绿水相辉映，构成了一幅古意盎然的风景画。这座精巧别致、清灵毓秀的"观音桥"，始建于清代乾隆年间，现桥于清道光二十年（1840年）建成，桥长23米、宽5.1米、拱跨12米，南北走向，全桥10个开间，计44根木柱。桥屋面双坡顶，中间升出重檐为牌楼式歇山屋顶，形成三重檐桥屋，鹊尾脊，四周飞檐翘角。观音桥的桥架结构属于八字支撑，即主结构由一组直铺横木，下面一组八字支撑组成，适用于跨度比较小的桥体，但似乎承重更好。整座桥的梁柱用料非常厚重，雕饰也比较精。
projects.content_en: Strangely, at the border between Shouning County and Zhouning County in northern Fujian, Shouning County has a wedge-shaped area extending into Zhouning County. I don't know what subtlety lies in this jurisdictional division; in any case, on the road from Zhouning to Shouning, one accidentally enters Shouning territory and unknowingly exits again. By the roadside in this area, we偶然 discovered a little-known eight-brace timber covered bridge hidden in deep mountains. I thought it was in Zhouning territory, only later learning it was the first covered bridge we were fortunate to see upon entering Shouning, the hometown of covered bridges. It looks very similar to several covered bridges in Chunchi Town, Zhouning County, such as Sanxian Bridge, Qixian Bridge, and Yuanlin Bridge. The entire bridge structure is reasonable, well-proportioned, and well-preserved, harmonizing with green mountains and clear waters to form a painting full of ancient charm. This exquisite and elegant "Guanyin Bridge" was founded during the Qianlong reign of the Qing; the current bridge was completed in 1840 (the 20th year of Daoguang reign). It is 23 meters long, 5.1 meters wide, with an arch span of 12 meters, running north-south, with 10 bays and 44 timber columns. The bridge roof has a double-slope top, with a double-eave archway-style hip-and-gable roof rising in the middle, forming a triple-eave bridge house, with magpie-tail ridges and flying upturned corners all around. Guanyin Bridge's frame structure belongs to the eight-brace type: the main structure consists of a set of directly laid transverse timbers with a set of eight-shaped braces below, suitable for bridges with smaller spans but seemingly better load-bearing. The beams and columns of the entire bridge are very thick, and the carvings are also quite refined.

projects.name: 红军桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县犀溪乡李家山村
projects.address_en: Lijiashan Village, Xixi Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
1937年红军抢渡历史
五角星状风雨板洞
projects.content_zh: 杨梅州风景名胜区，风景在云雾中似乎只是传说。雨后逐渐放晴，车行在寿宁县到红军桥所在的犀溪乡李家村的省道上，一路上领略风光无限。到了小村李家山，有熟悉的石铺古道穿村而过，我们知道它通向哪里。看着古道，不禁想起周宁县后垅桥的那一段，此处的古道有过之而无不及，而且距离也比较长，从村中将近1公里都是保存完好、延续不断。照此看来，此处的红军桥虽是20世纪50年代重建的，那么在此之前的那座桥是否也是木拱廊桥？如果是的话一定是规模宏大，年代久远。1937年3月12日，山洪暴发冲毁木桥，住在李家山村的红军将士范式人、许威等24人遭国民党军队和民团的围捕。此时，李家山的9位地下交通员，连夜赶制木筏，把他们抢渡过河。1954年福安专区副专员许威拨款建木拱桥，群众取名红军桥。红军桥两端桥堍用河卵石砌筑。长42.2米，宽5.1米，拱跨32.6米。南北走向，15开间，64柱，上覆双坡顶。风雨板的板洞有的呈五角星状，是本桥相对其他廊桥绝无仅有的一大特色。
projects.content_en: Yangmeizhou Scenic Area — the scenery seems only legend in the clouds and mist. After the rain, it gradually cleared; driving on the provincial road from Shouning County to Lijiashan Village in Xixi Township where Red Army Bridge stands, we enjoyed boundless scenery along the way. Arriving at the small village Lijiashan, a familiar stone-paved ancient path runs through the village, and we know where it leads. Looking at the ancient path, I can't help recalling the section at Houlong Bridge in Zhouning County; the ancient path here is even better, and also longer — nearly 1 kilometer from the village is well-preserved and continuous. It seems that although Red Army Bridge here was rebuilt in the 1950s, was the previous bridge also a timber-arch covered bridge? If so, it must have been large in scale and ancient in date. On March 12, 1937, a mountain torrent destroyed the timber bridge. Red Army soldiers Fan Shiren, Xu Wei, and 22 others living in Lijiashan Village were besieged by Kuomintang troops and militia. At that time, 9 underground couriers from Lijiashan hurriedly built rafts overnight to ferry them across the river. In 1954, Xu Wei, deputy commissioner of the Fu'an Special District, allocated funds to build a timber-arch bridge, which the people named Red Army Bridge. Both ends of Red Army Bridge are built with river pebbles. It is 42.2 meters long, 5.1 meters wide, with an arch span of 32.6 meters. Running north-south, it has 15 bays and 64 columns, covered by a double-slope roof. Some holes in the wind-and-rain boards are star-shaped — a unique feature of this bridge compared to other covered bridges.

projects.name: 鸾峰桥
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县下党乡下党村
projects.address_en: Xiadang Village, Xiadang Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
迁建与保存
木拱廊桥中第一雄桥
拱跨37.6米
金字塔形巨石
projects.content_zh: 天气阴沉沉的，仿佛要下雨，踏上寻访鸾峰桥之路。去下党村路况不是很好，或许因为走的人太少的缘故，让山洪冲坏了，新修的路段全改用水泥了。路上有标识："此路段尚未验收，限速15公里，否则后果自负。"好在山色依然。从芹洋乡到下党乡的十几公里是一段非常"武侠"的路段，适合拍武侠电影。右手是奔腾的长濑溪，左手是峭壁。一路上绝少有人，打开车窗，不时有溪水飞落而下，传来哗哗的水声，又飞快远去，其景真如画境。路过一个水库，远远看到一座廊桥横跨深涧之上，甚是壮观。经查问，这座桥是被迁建的长濑溪桥，真是意外之喜。主角鸾峰桥堪称木拱廊桥中第一雄桥，桥长47.6米，宽4.9米，拱跨37.6米，北面桥堍建在岩石上，南面桥堍用块石砌筑。廊屋幽深，四柱九檩，抬梁式木架构，17间72柱。鸾峰桥外观端庄，顶部无装饰，弧度不明显，侧视桥顶有如俯卧的巨龙。鸾峰桥周边环境奇美，不但有奇峰，更引人注目的是桥下的巨大怪石。还有一块外形酷似金字塔的巨石。鸾峰桥与金字塔遥相呼应，一个200年，一个200万年，她俩有的聊吗？
projects.content_en: The weather was overcast, as if about to rain, as we set out on the road to find Luanfeng Bridge. The road to Xiadang Village is not very good — perhaps because too few people travel it, it was damaged by mountain torrents, and the newly repaired sections are all concrete. There is a sign on the road: "This road section has not been inspected; speed limit 15 km/h, otherwise consequences are your own responsibility." Fortunately, the mountain scenery remains. The dozen or so kilometers from Qinyang Township to Xiadang Township is a very "wuxia" (martial arts) section, suitable for filming martial arts movies. On the right is the rushing Changlai Stream, on the left are cliffs. Along the way there are almost no people; opening the car window, stream water occasionally falls down with a rushing sound, then speeds away — the scene is truly like a painting. Passing a reservoir, we saw from afar a covered bridge spanning a deep ravine, quite spectacular. Upon inquiry, this bridge is the relocated Changlaixi Bridge — a truly unexpected delight. The main attraction, Luanfeng Bridge, can be called the number one majestic bridge among timber-arch covered bridges: 47.6 meters long, 4.9 meters wide, with an arch span of 37.6 meters. The north abutment is built on rock, the south abutment with dressed stone. The covered hall is deep and secluded, with four columns and nine purlins, beam-lifting timber frame, 17 bays and 72 columns. Luanfeng Bridge has a dignified appearance, no decoration on top, with unobvious curvature; viewed from the side, the bridge top resembles a prone giant dragon. The surrounding environment of Luanfeng Bridge is wondrously beautiful: not only are there strange peaks, but more eye-catching are the huge strange rocks below the bridge. There is also a giant rock shaped exactly like a pyramid. Luanfeng Bridge and the pyramid echo each other from afar — one 200 years old, one 2 million years old — do they have things to talk about?

projects.name: 小东上桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县坑底乡小东村
projects.address_en: Xiaodong Village, Kengdi Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
清嘉庆六年建
内部木工令人惊讶
projects.content_zh: 小东上桥，距大宝桥仅数百米，小桥流水，绿树黄花，别有一番意境。此桥清嘉庆六年（1801年）建，桥长21.4米，宽4.6米，拱跨16.4米，东西走向。两边桥台用河卵石砌筑。桥架可见三节苗7根。桥屋8开间，36柱。上覆双坡顶，桥中神龛祀观音。梁架选材厚重，上面墨书建桥时间、工匠名等资料。大有大的难处，小有小的长处，看看此桥内部的木工，令人惊讶。小东村一上一下两座桥各有特色，大宝桥的体量与其下面的小河不太相称，而这座小东上桥内部的木工又与其较小的外观不太相称，既然小东下桥叫大宝，不如这座小东上桥就叫小宝如何？县文物局答应吗？
projects.content_en: Xiaodongshang Bridge is only a few hundred meters from Dabao Bridge, with small bridges, flowing water, green trees and yellow flowers — a unique atmosphere. This bridge was built in 1801 (the sixth year of Jiaqing reign, Qing). It is 21.4 meters long, 4.6 meters wide, with an arch span of 16.4 meters, running east-west. Both abutments are built with river pebbles. The frame shows 7 three-section miao timbers. The bridge house has 8 bays and 36 columns, covered by a double-slope roof, with a shrine in the middle enshrining Guanyin. The beam frame uses thick materials, with ink inscriptions of the bridge-building date and craftsman names. Big has its difficulties, small has its advantages — looking at the woodwork inside this bridge is surprising. The upper and lower bridges of Xiaodong Village each have their characteristics: Dabao Bridge's scale is mismatched with the small stream below, while the interior woodwork of this Xiaodongshang Bridge is mismatched with its smaller exterior. Since Xiaodong Lower Bridge is called Dabao (Great Treasure), why not call this Xiaodong Upper Bridge Xiaobao (Little Treasure)? Will the county cultural heritage bureau agree?

projects.name: 杨梅洲桥
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县坑底乡杨梅洲村东北1公里
projects.address_en: 1 km northeast of Yangmeizhou Village, Kengdi Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
虎造桥传说
1939年重建
雁齿小红桥
projects.content_zh: 杨梅洲桥在水的那边，与红军桥属于不同的乡，两桥相距仅8公里，但这8公里还没有铺水泥，全是尖利的碎石。离开红军桥执意往杨梅洲桥而去，路过一小村庄，居然有大姐给我一小袋东西要我帮忙"寄"往杨梅洲村，我正困惑如何与那接货人联系，大姐说是她已经打过电话了。后来果然没有走错路，因为山路狭窄崎岖根本别无他路可走，而且到了村头马上有人过来接货。杨梅洲村虽地处旅游旺地，但比想象的要小而清静。当地路况人情由此可见一斑。杨梅洲桥名雁齿小红桥，建于乾隆六年（1741年），乾隆五十六年（1791年）、道光二十一年（1841年）、同治十七年（1869年）曾修。现桥为1939年重建。相传，最后一次造桥时，匠师将梁木横放竖摆，量时吻合，架时短尺，几次三番总难造起，一日再次将梁木上架欲造时，忽闻峡间虎啸如雷，匠师逃生离去，梁木便纷纷坠落，谁料榫人卯窍，天工巧成。因此，该桥又有"虎造桥"之称。杨梅洲桥无疑属于大型廊桥，顶部无装饰，但弧度做得自然漂亮。桥架三节苗大。
projects.content_en: Yangmeizhou Bridge is on the other side of the water, belonging to a different township from Red Army Bridge, only 8 kilometers apart — but these 8 kilometers are not yet paved with concrete, all sharp gravel. Leaving Red Army Bridge and insisting on going to Yangmeizhou Bridge, passing a small village, a middle-aged woman actually gave me a small bag of things to help "mail" to Yangmeizhou Village. I was wondering how to contact the recipient, but she said she had already called. Later, indeed I didn't take the wrong road, because the narrow, rugged mountain road had no other path, and upon arriving at the village head someone immediately came to receive the goods. Though Yangmeizhou Village is in a tourist hotspot, it is smaller and quieter than imagined. The local road conditions and human kindness are evident from this. Yangmeizhou Bridge, named "Goose-tooth Little Red Bridge," was built in 1741 (the sixth year of Qianlong reign), and repaired in 1791 (the 56th year of Qianlong), 1841 (the 21st year of Daoguang), and 1869 (the 17th year of Tongzhi). The current bridge was rebuilt in 1939. According to legend, during the last bridge-building, the master craftsman placed the beams horizontally and vertically — they matched when measured but were short when erected. After repeated failures, one day when again trying to erect the beams, a tiger's roar like thunder suddenly came from the gorge; the craftsmen fled for their lives, and the beams fell one after another — unexpectedly, the tenons fit into the mortises perfectly, as if crafted by heaven. Hence the bridge is also called "Tiger-Built Bridge." Yangmeizhou Bridge undoubtedly belongs to the large covered bridge category, with no decoration on top, but the curvature is naturally beautiful. The frame's three-section miao timbers are large.

projects.name: 尤溪桥
projects.address: 宁德寿宁县芹洋乡尤溪村东
projects.address_en: East of Youxi Village, Qinyang Township, Shouning County, Ningde
highlights: 斗拱
拆换下来的老构件
偶遇廊桥
projects.content_zh: 就要离开廊桥之乡寿宁，奔政和县而去，心中颇有不舍，而且难走的路要再走一遍，情绪不是太高，突然此老赫然出现在眼前。在一个看似脏乱的不起眼的小村落的公路边，她突然出现在我的眼前。说实在的作为一个喜欢廊桥的人，每次去寻访廊桥都要做不少准备工作，一旦有机会偶遇一二，总是难掩兴奋。可这次没来由地竟有些伤感，就那么在车里坐了半天看着此桥。她仿佛一个年老色衰的女人，幽怨地。
projects.content_en: About to leave Shouning, the hometown of covered bridges, heading for Zhenghe County, I felt quite reluctant, and having to traverse the difficult road again put me in a low mood — when suddenly this old one appeared before my eyes. By the roadside of a seemingly messy, inconspicuous small village, she suddenly appeared before me. Honestly, as someone who loves covered bridges, every visit requires much preparation; once there is an opportunity to encounter one by chance, excitement is hard to conceal. But this time, for no reason, I felt somewhat sad, just sitting in the car for half a day looking at this bridge. She is like an aging woman, melancholic.

projects.name: 八蒲村
projects.address: 宁德周宁县七步镇八蒲村
projects.address_en: Bapu Village, Qibu Town, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 村落格局与环境
木结构
石作做法
黄墙黑瓦
河两岸泾渭分明
商品流通集散地
projects.content_zh: 寻访周宁县的省级文保建筑登龙桥有意外之喜。登龙桥左近隐藏着一个可爱的古村，虽说是名不见经传，但因其建筑规划的风格统一和到目前为止保存完好而别具特色。登龙桥所跨的小河将八蒲小村一分为二，或者反过来说，沿河的两岸都建有村落。河的这一边，老房子的外墙有夯土的，也有木制的；河的另一边豁然开朗，风光为之一变，院落井然，木结构则喜用斗拱。当地盛产这种外形兼具鸡鸭特长的吉祥鸟，一点不怕人。或者因为村中见不到一个人，只有建筑静静伫立。村中的房屋风格统一，是在山地流行的黄色墙面，配以黑色屋顶，比起沿海平原地区的建筑多了几分质朴。站在高处远眺，村中的新建筑几乎全都集中在河对岸，河的这一边全都是老建筑，成片的黄墙黑瓦，不见一个"炮楼"，不见一个"水泥墩子"，不知道在万物疯狂生长的今天，八蒲小村何来如此智慧和能力，把自己的家园规划保护得这么好？仔细琢磨一番，可能也与自古而来的风俗风水的影响有关系。八蒲自古作为一个村子，同时也是商品的流通集散地，穿村而过的古道和村头的廊桥可作为佐证。那么很有可能务农读书的住在河的这一边，经商贩运的住在河的那一边，可谓泾渭分明。到后来演变成要居家守成的住这边，想发财的住河那一边，而当下大家都想发财，所以新建筑就都集中在河对岸了。放眼登龙桥，感觉自然而然，仿佛它不是人建造的，而是自己从村中长出来的。是的，有这样的古村，必然有这样的廊桥，古村的风貌依旧，廊桥自然也保护得历久弥新。但不知主宰这一切的精神力量是什么？
projects.content_en: Visiting Denglong Bridge, a provincial-level cultural heritage building in Zhouning County, brought an unexpected delight. Near Denglong Bridge hides a lovely ancient village; though little-known, it is distinctive for its unified architectural planning and well-preserved state to date. The small river crossed by Denglong Bridge divides Bapu Village in two — or conversely, villages are built on both banks along the river. On this side of the river, old houses have rammed-earth or wooden exterior walls; on the other side, the view opens up, the scenery changes, courtyards are orderly, and timber structures favor bracket sets (dougong). The local area abounds in this auspicious bird with the combined features of chickens and ducks, quite unafraid of people. Or perhaps because not a single person is seen in the village, only buildings stand quietly. The houses in the village are unified in style: yellow walls popular in mountainous areas, paired with black roofs, more rustic than buildings in coastal plains. Looking from a high vantage point, the village's new buildings are almost all concentrated on the opposite bank, while this side is entirely old buildings — clusters of yellow walls and black tiles, without a single "blockhouse" or "concrete block." I wonder how, in today's world of rampant growth, Bapu Village has such wisdom and ability to plan and protect its homeland so well. Upon reflection, it may also relate to the influence of ancient customs and fengshui. Bapu has always been a village and also a commodity distribution hub, evidenced by the ancient path running through the village and the covered bridge at its head. It is likely that those who farmed and studied lived on this side of the river, while those who traded and transported lived on the other side — clearly divided. Later it evolved: those who wanted to maintain the family home lived on this side, those who wanted to get rich lived on the other side; and now everyone wants to get rich, so new buildings are all concentrated on the opposite bank. Looking at Denglong Bridge, it feels natural, as if it was not built by people but grew out of the village itself. Yes, with such an ancient village, there must be such a covered bridge; the ancient village's appearance remains, and the covered bridge is naturally preserved and renewed over time. But I wonder what spiritual force governs all this?

projects.name: 登龙桥
projects.address: 宁德周宁县七步镇八蒲村
projects.address_en: Bapu Village, Qibu Town, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
石砌桥架
青砖铺桥面防火
梁柱题跋极多
projects.content_zh: 在闽北的山区驾车永远是画中游，无论天气如何，所谓淡妆浓妆总相宜。寻访周宁县境内的登龙桥，一路从福安到周宁的公路景色也自不待言。公路边有这样不起眼的廊桥，默默立于山水之间，连接过去的古商道。小桥的桥架是石砌的，不是木拱。登桥小憩，又是一桥外青山古画屏。登龙桥始建年代不详，清康熙二十六年（1687年）水毁后，于清康熙五十六年（1717年）八蒲村民黄宠等募建；乾隆三十九年（1774年）生员黄廷元等募修；道光十六年（1836年）武生黄高捷、张仕光重建，1986年村民饰修。木桥长38米，宽4.9米，单孔净跨23.5米，离水高9米，全桥杉木建造。外观端庄朴实，建筑上没有过多的装饰，廊屋全封闭，给人以厚重的感觉，可能也与山区气温较低需要保温有关。桥面木板上铺砌青砖以防火。桥上建单檐硬山顶廊屋，15开间，高4.5米，桥中通道宽3.2米，两边设坐板。登龙桥梁柱之上的题跋极多，而且字迹大多清晰如新。桥头有石砌台阶，连接古道。此桥2005年被省人民政府列为省级重点文物保护单位。2006在本可以被国务院列为全国重点文物保护单位，只因该县没有文物经费，没能完成绘图任务，最终没有上报。同批申报的周边县的木拱桥2006年都被国务院列为全国重点文物保护单位了，这可是周宁县的一大损失。目前浙江省将此项目申报世遗预备名录。无论你申报还是不申报，它就在那里。
projects.content_en: Driving in the mountainous areas of northern Fujian is always like traveling in a painting, no matter the weather — as the saying goes, both light and heavy makeup suit it. Visiting Denglong Bridge in Zhouning County, the scenery along the highway from Fu'an to Zhouning goes without saying. By the roadside stands such an inconspicuous covered bridge, silently standing among mountains and waters, connecting the ancient trade routes of the past. The small bridge's frame is stone-built, not timber arch. Resting on the bridge, one sees yet another ancient painting screen of green mountains beyond. Denglong Bridge's founding date is unknown. After being destroyed by flood in 1687 (the 26th year of Kangxi reign), it was rebuilt through fundraising by Huang Chong and other villagers of Bapu in 1717 (the 56th year of Kangxi); repaired through fundraising by student Huang Tingyuan and others in 1774 (the 39th year of Qianlong); rebuilt by military students Huang Gaojie and Zhang Shiguang in 1836 (the 16th year of Daoguang); and decorated by villagers in 1986. The timber bridge is 38 meters long, 4.9 meters wide, with a single clear span of 23.5 meters and 9 meters above the water, entirely built of Chinese fir. Its appearance is dignified and plain, without excessive decoration; the covered hall is fully enclosed, giving a heavy feeling — perhaps related to the need for insulation in the cooler mountain temperatures. Blue bricks are laid on the wooden deck to prevent fire. On the bridge stands a single-eave gable-roof covered hall, 15 bays, 4.5 meters high, with a 3.2-meter-wide central passage and benches on both sides. There are numerous inscriptions on Denglong Bridge's beams and columns, most of which are as clear as new. At the bridgehead are stone steps connecting to the ancient path. This bridge was listed as a provincial key cultural heritage site by the provincial people's government in 2005. In 2006, it could have been listed as a national key cultural heritage site by the State Council, but because the county had no cultural heritage funding, it failed to complete the drawing task and ultimately did not submit. The timber-arch bridges of neighboring counties submitted in the same batch were all listed as national key cultural heritage sites in 2006 — this is a great loss for Zhouning County. Currently, Zhejiang Province has submitted this project to the World Heritage tentative list. Whether you submit it or not, it is right there.

projects.name: 后垅村
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德周宁县礼门乡后垅村
projects.address_en: Houlong Village, Limen Township, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 村落格局与环境
木结构
石作做法
风水绝佳
古商道石拱桥
清澈甘甜泉水
projects.content_zh: 从县城进入周宁西南部的大山之中寻访后垅桥，一路有很多朴素而有特色的小村。大山中的小村溪兜村，静静地安卧于公路下边，整个村子的风格统一，错落有致，远处可见新建的祠堂或庙宇。再往深山中行去，首洞村中全部是老房子了。这一地区房屋的风格类似，就是没有什么风格，但连接成片看去，别有风味。后垅村没什么名气，也不是历史文化名村，但因为地处偏僻，交通不便，反而免受现代气息的干扰，保存如此完好，令人感叹。另外后垅村的风水绝佳，看看眼前的那个圆滚滚的大山包，气度非凡。现在村子沉寂了，以前可是商业要道，有古道廊桥为证。古商道跨越村头的小溪，修建了这样一座外形美观规模不小的石拱桥，可见当初村子的富足。漫步村中，在小巷中穿行，没有见到什么人，有些院落街门大开，有些老宅看上去已经明显荒废，但打开院中的龙头，居然还流出清澈甘甜的泉水，有的院中看似无人居住，但地上满是鞭炮屑，看来老屋在春节时还是凝聚族人的场。
projects.content_en: Entering the great mountains of southwestern Zhouning from the county seat to visit Houlong Bridge, there are many simple yet distinctive small villages along the way. Xidou Village, a small village in the mountains, lies quietly below the highway, with a unified style and well-arranged layout; newly built ancestral halls or temples can be seen in the distance. Going deeper into the mountains, Shoudong Village is entirely old houses. The houses in this region are similar in style — that is, no particular style — but seen connected together, they have a unique flavor. Houlong Village is not famous, nor is it a historical and cultural village, but because of its remote location and inconvenient transportation, it has instead been spared from modern interference and preserved so well —令人感叹. Moreover, Houlong Village has excellent fengshui: look at that round, plump mountain包 before us, extraordinary in presence. Now the village is quiet, but it was once a commercial thoroughfare, evidenced by the ancient path and covered bridge. The ancient trade route crosses the stream at the village head, with such a beautiful and sizable stone arch bridge built — showing the village's former prosperity. Wandering the village, threading through alleys, we saw few people; some courtyard gates were wide open, some old houses looked clearly abandoned, but turning on the dragon-head faucet in the courtyard, clear and sweet spring water actually flowed out. Some courtyards seemed uninhabited, but the ground was covered with firecracker debris — it seems the old houses still serve as gathering places for clans during Spring Festival.

projects.name: 后垅桥
projects.address: 宁德周宁县礼门乡后垅村
projects.address_en: Houlong Village, Limen Township, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
跨度30米大型险峻型木拱廊桥
石凿护栏古道
城堡城门洞
projects.content_zh: 后垅桥位于周宁县礼门乡后垅（垄）村，周宁县与屏南县交界的山谷里面。因为地处相对偏僻，如果电子地图的导航不能直达，就先导航到名叫"八角亭"的村庄，面前两条路，直走上坡，右转下坡，走右转下坡的那条路再翻过一座大山就到后垅村。一路上风景无法说了，路面尚好，但山高坡险，有时候甚至分不清是在开汽车还是开飞机，有恐高症的慎入吧，不过坚持有坚持的补偿。村头小溪上的石拱桥连接着一条古道，根据以往的经验，古道通向廊桥，所以也就没太多犹豫便沿古道而上。古道应是当初屏南通往周宁的商道，宽度比先前见过的古道都要宽，看来规格不低。有的地方是在山间的巨石上直接凿出台阶，有的地方还留有石头凿成的护栏，这也是先前很少见的。从石栏的风蚀程度看，年代相当久远，如果那时此地就造有廊桥的话，廊桥的年代应至少早于清代。后垅桥始建年代不详，清乾隆年曾重修，咸丰年间重建，现桥重建于1964年。后垅桥的跨度很大达30米，总长34米，距水面近20米，属于不折不扣的大型险峻型木拱廊桥，与屏南境内的百祥桥、龙井桥属于同一规格。桥的外形端庄，但不失灵动，顶部做成优美的弧线，两边翘角，中间装饰有小宝塔。奇怪的是宝塔上插有祈福的草棍，不知道是什么人冒着危险插上去的。整个桥的风雨板全封闭，保存完好。桥架结构三节苗9根，但从这个角度看去用材稍显细窄，外形也欠规整，是否和重修时木材比较短缺有关？桥屋地面用砖铺就，看上去应该是旧砖重修时再利用了。桥屋13间56柱，整体感觉规整，做工讲究，窥窗形式多样。桥内的梁柱上写满题跋，以捐资人姓名为主。桥虽是解放后重修的，但仍沿用旧制，主办人、建造人、捐款人都写得很清楚。以前的"恭祝当今皇上万寿无疆"亦改成了"中华人民共和国万岁"。桥的另一端也有古道，古道边也有护栏，难得的是还有残存的类似古堡的城门洞。光是这样的城堡就够文物保护资格了，这么多的古迹聚集一处真是难能可贵，当年此地之重要可见一斑。躺在古道上，一切尽收眼底。空气如此清澈，很远的景物就恍然近在眼前。耳边除了风声和鸟鸣，听不到一点声音。望着对面山崖上的古树，似乎领略到一点中国山水画的意境。不知道眼前的后垅桥能否入画？如果可以的话，比《清明上河图》那座廊桥如何？所不同的是那座桥上挤满了人，这座桥上一人没有。
projects.content_en: Houlong Bridge is located in Houlong Village, Limen Township, Zhouning County, in the valley at the border of Zhouning and Pingnan counties. Because it is relatively remote, if electronic map navigation cannot reach it directly, first navigate to the village called "Bajiaoting." Before you are two roads: straight ahead goes uphill, right turn goes downhill — take the right-turn downhill road, cross another great mountain, and you arrive at Houlong Village. The scenery along the way is beyond description; the road surface is okay, but the mountains are high and slopes dangerous — sometimes one can't even tell whether driving a car or flying a plane. Those with acrophobia should be cautious, but persistence has its rewards. The stone arch bridge over the stream at the village head connects to an ancient path; based on past experience, ancient paths lead to covered bridges, so without much hesitation we followed the ancient path upward. This ancient path should have been the trade route from Pingnan to Zhouning, wider than any ancient path seen before — apparently of high specification. In some places, steps were directly chiseled into giant mountain rocks; in others, stone-carved railings remain, also rarely seen before. From the weathering of the stone railings, the age is quite ancient; if covered bridges were built here then, the bridge should date at least earlier than the Qing. Houlong Bridge's founding date is unknown; it was restored during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, rebuilt during the Xianfeng reign, and the current bridge was rebuilt in 1964. Houlong Bridge has a large span of 30 meters, total length 34 meters, nearly 20 meters above the water — a truly large and precipitous timber-arch covered bridge, of the same specification as Baixiang Bridge and Longjing Bridge in Pingnan. The bridge's appearance is dignified yet lively, with the top forming a beautiful arc, upturned corners on both sides, and a small pagoda decoration in the middle. Strangely, prayer grass sticks are inserted on the pagoda — I don't know who risked climbing up to place them. The entire bridge's wind-and-rain boards are fully enclosed and well-preserved. The frame structure has 9 three-section miao timbers, but from this angle the materials appear slightly thin and narrow, and the外形 less regular — perhaps related to timber shortages during reconstruction? The bridge house floor is paved with bricks, apparently old bricks reused during restoration. The bridge house has 13 bays and 56 columns, overall feeling regular, with exquisite workmanship and varied window forms. The beams and columns inside are covered with inscriptions, mainly donor names. Though rebuilt after liberation, the old system was followed: organizers, builders, and donors are all clearly written. The former "Wishing the Current Emperor Longevity" was also changed to "Long Live the People's Republic of China." At the other end of the bridge is also an ancient path with railings; rare is the remaining castle-like gate opening. Such a castle alone qualifies for cultural heritage protection; so many relics gathered in one place is truly precious, showing the importance of this place in former times. Lying on the ancient path, everything comes into view. The air is so clear that distant scenery seems close at hand. Besides wind and birdsong, not a sound is heard. Looking at the ancient trees on the opposite cliff, one seems to grasp a bit of the artistic conception of Chinese landscape painting. I wonder if Houlong Bridge before us could enter a painting? If so, how does it compare with the covered bridge in "Along the River During the Qingming Festival"? The difference is that bridge was crowded with people, while this one has not a soul.

projects.name: 林公祖殿
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 福建省周宁县玛坑乡杉洋村
projects.address_en: Shanyang Village, Makeng Township, Zhouning County, Fujian
highlights: 斗拱
拆换下来的老构件
明正德八年大殿
清嘉庆钟鼓楼太子亭
三重檐面貌
林公忠平王
projects.content_zh: 海上谋生的人拜妈祖，居家的人求助于"救产护胎佑民"的"顺天圣母"陈靖姑，而无论在家与否健康平安都是最重要的，所以我们能够见到慈济宫中的吴夲，还有这里的林公。林公名祖亘，南宋庆元三年（1197年）生人，不凡之处在于发明神铳和精通药理，普救众生。这几位普通人终于成神，靠的其实不是法力，而是大众的向往。林公忠平王祖殿冠带形河水的凸曲之处，背山而建，坐南向北。整体布局为一核心院落加二侧院；核心院落前有山门，回廊紧凑，上设钟鼓二楼，大殿巍峨，是所有建筑的依托；二侧院之内仅有配殿，结构简明，反而烘托出大殿的壮观。大殿，即祖殿，建于明正德八年（1513年），面阔五间，进深四间，抬梁穿斗混合木构架，单层，歇山顶，尺度宏大；正脊装饰双龙戏珠，四角起翘饰蟠螭；殿内中央设斗拱藻井，神龛祭林公泥塑，内藏忠平王遗骸；殿前小巧的钟鼓二楼，也为重檐歇山顶，清嘉庆十年（1805年）所成；门楼造型复杂，更有清嘉庆十年在门楼正上方增建太子亭，形成今日三重檐的面貌；祖殿之左右院中的配殿建于明代，毁于"文革"期间，近年在原址重建；配殿东侧为古时的客栈，门右边有宣统二年（1910年）八都馆乞首吴大妹立《禁乞碑》一通。尝惜年近品低，有意无意地贬低清代以来的细碎；今反观林公祖殿，嘉庆所加钟鼓楼和太子亭，恰恰是轮点睛的妙笔，不仅给一座普通的大庙添加了丰富的轮廓线，而且利用尺度对比的手法夸大了祖殿的规模。时代固有自己的风气，但是在大匠手里，也是可以生花的。
projects.content_en: Those who make a living at sea worship Mazu; those who stay home seek help from Chen Jinggu, the "Holy Mother of Heaven" who "saves childbirth, protects fetuses, and blesses the people." Whether at home or away, health and peace are most important — so we see Wu Ben in Ciji Palace, and here Lin Gong. Lin Gong, named Zugen, was born in 1197 (the third year of Qingyuan reign, Southern Song). His extraordinariness lay in inventing the divine musket and mastering pharmacology, universally saving sentient beings. These ordinary people finally became gods, relying not on magical power but on the aspirations of the masses. Lin Gong Zhongping Wang's Ancestral Temple is built at the convex curve of the belt-shaped river, backed by mountains, facing north. The overall layout is one core courtyard plus two side courtyards; the core courtyard has a gate in front, compact surrounding corridors, with bell and drum towers above, and the majestic main hall as the anchor of all buildings; the two side courtyards contain only auxiliary halls, with simple structure that反而 sets off the main hall's grandeur. The main hall, i.e., the ancestral hall, was built in 1513 (the eighth year of Zhengde reign, Ming), five bays wide and four deep, with a mixed beam-lifting and column-and-tie timber frame, single story, hip-and-gable roof, grand in scale; the main ridge is decorated with two dragons playing with a pearl, and the four upturned corners are decorated with panchi (mythical creatures); in the center of the hall stands a bracket-set caisson ceiling, with a shrine enshrining a clay statue of Lin Gong, containing the remains of King Zhongping; the small bell and drum towers in front of the hall are also double-eave hip-and-gable roofs, completed in 1805 (the tenth year of Jiaqing reign, Qing); the gate tower has a complex shape, and in 1805 a Taizi Pavilion was added directly above the gate tower, forming today's triple-eave appearance; the auxiliary halls in the left and right courtyards of the ancestral hall were built in the Ming, destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and recently rebuilt on the original site; east of the auxiliary halls was an ancient inn, and to the right of the gate stands a "Begging Prohibition Stele" erected by Wu Damei, head of the Badu Inn, in 1910 (the second year of Xuantong). I once regretted that later periods produced lower-quality work, consciously or unconsciously belittling the intricacies since the Qing; now looking back at Lin Gong Ancestral Temple, the bell and drum towers and Taizi Pavilion added in the Jiaqing reign are precisely the finishing touches — not only adding rich silhouette lines to an ordinary large temple, but also using scale contrast to exaggerate the ancestral hall's规模. Each era has its own style, but in the hands of a master craftsman, it can also bloom.

projects.name: 三仙桥
projects.address: 宁德周宁县纯池镇禾溪村
projects.address_en: Hexi Village, Chunchi Town, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
明成化三年始建
藻井彩画1920年
村中廊桥女性化
projects.content_zh: 临水而建的禾溪村，像她的名字一样美。村规模甚大，而且至今保存完好，没有什么太扎眼的现代建筑破坏景观。如果有时间沿着村中阡陌纵横的小道漫步而去，一定是摄影爱好者的天堂。三仙桥于明成化三年（1467年）始建，1917年加宽重建。桥长18.4米，宽5.4米，桥屋7开间，用36根杉木柱，穿斗式木构架，双坡顶。藻井彩画绘于1920年。桥正中和两端均另建四坡顶桥屋。大桥两端建有门亭。桥屋内部比较宽大，适合更多人聚集。三仙桥这种形制的廊桥在这一带比较流行，由于建在村中而非深涧大溪之上，因此显得更女性化一些，祝祷、聚会、休闲的功能更重要，而非单纯的交通功能，桥架的规模较小，而桥屋的建制、装潢占得比重较大。绿树掩映，依山傍水，要是等到月上东山，在桥屋里摆上几杯清酒，透过此窗赏月，该是何景？距三仙桥所在的禾溪村5公里左右有一个小村名叫桃坑，那里有三仙桥的姊妹桥七仙桥，原名栏新桥，建制与三仙桥差不多，只是目前已经被装饰一新。老的制式显得多么的典雅，华丽与内敛并存，尽显雍容之气。幸亏网络上有老照片，我们还能知道七仙桥原来的样子，为什么物质越发达品味反而趋于庸俗，一个个张牙舞爪的？或许现在我们看到的物质发达原本也算不得什么发达，差远了，真正的物质发达不是这个样子。桃坑村附近的山上有一胜境，千年古刹灵峰寺。那时日近黄昏，寺中空旷没有香客，只有梵乐伴着寺中修士们高声的诵经声。
projects.content_en: Hexi Village, built by the water, is as beautiful as its name. The village is quite large and well-preserved to this day, without too many glaring modern buildings spoiling the scenery. If one has time to wander along the crisscrossing paths in the village, it must be a paradise for photography enthusiasts. Sanxian Bridge (Bridge of Three Immortals) was first built in 1467 (the third year of Chenghua reign, Ming) and widened and rebuilt in 1917. It is 18.4 meters long, 5.4 meters wide, with a 7-bay bridge house using 36 Chinese fir columns, column-and-tie timber frame, double-slope roof. The caisson ceiling paintings were done in 1920. Four-slope roof bridge houses are additionally built at the center and both ends of the bridge. Gate pavilions stand at both ends of the bridge. The interior of the bridge house is relatively spacious, suitable for larger gatherings. Covered bridges of this type are popular in this region; because they are built in villages rather than over deep ravines and large streams, they appear more feminine, with functions of prayer, gathering, and leisure more important than mere transportation — the frame scale is smaller, while the bridge house's construction and decoration account for a larger proportion. Shaded by green trees, nestled by mountains and water — if one waits until the moon rises over the eastern mountain, sets out a few cups of clear wine in the bridge house, and admires the moon through this window, what a scene it would be! About 5 kilometers from Hexi Village where Sanxian Bridge stands is a small village called Taokeng, where there is Sanxian Bridge's sister bridge, Qixian Bridge (Bridge of Seven Immortals), originally named Lanxin Bridge, with similar construction to Sanxian Bridge, only now it has been newly decorated. How elegant the old system appears, with splendor and restraint coexisting, fully showing dignified grace. Fortunately, old photos exist online, so we can still know Qixian Bridge's original appearance. Why does more material development lead to more vulgar taste, all aggressive and clawing? Perhaps the material development we see now doesn't count as development at all — it's far from it; true material development is not like this. On the mountain near Taokeng Village is a scenic spot: the thousand-year-old ancient temple Lingfeng Temple. It was near dusk, the temple was empty with no pilgrims, only Buddhist music accompanying the loud chanting of the temple's practitioners.

projects.name: 院林桥
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德周宁县纯池镇
projects.address_en: Chunchi Town, Zhouning County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
八字叠交桥架
残破但风骨犹存
院林桥翰林出处
般若禅寺千年古刹
projects.content_zh: 在从三仙桥所在的禾溪村回往纯池镇的路边，偶遇此老。虽然已经残破不堪，但风骨犹存。桥屋的建制是当地流行的样式，和三仙桥如出一辙，可以想见当初的做工也是比较繁复。其桥架结构不是典型的编木叠交架构，而是八字叠交，就是一组是平直的横木，下面八字桥架加以支撑。桥架结构清晰可见，虽说此桥看着不高，与山间的那些大桥不可同日而语，但这个角度看上去还是有点晕。桥中有神龛，桥架曾经被毁，但依然坚固，留有一半可以行人。现在的样式倒是挺像建筑学院的教学模型，可以考虑说服一下清华校长，把此老请回校园如何？夕阳老去桥尚在，尤有佛光照半边。越看越觉得当初绝非等闲，不意竟沦落至此。偶遇二老，务农归来，见我在拍照，热情地向我宣讲此桥由来。据说此桥年代久远，远近闻名，本名"院林桥"，本乡有去赶考的学士都是要来此一拜的。后来年久失修，逐渐破败，前些年附近修水电站，此桥几乎被废，因当地村民据理力争，政府又在上游修一拦水坝，此桥才勉强得以保存。现在大家都想把桥修起来，但苦于没有经费。看来此"院林桥"的出处不凡，顾名思义应该是当地有人中了进士甚至点了翰林后修建此桥，以至于后来学生们赶考前都要来沾沾福气。至于说到修桥经费，以前修桥全都是自发集资，现在村中高楼林立，不像缺钱的样子，主要还是人们的观念在转变。此二老急公好义，听说我是来做古建筑调研，又领我去看桥边的一座千年古刹，始建时距今已经有1300多年历史，比唐还要早。此般若禅寺20世纪80年代曾经重修，哪知好事多磨，先是上游修水电站，寺院几乎被淹，后来又是邻村的人们因为风水的问题，与本村的人们起了极大的争执，闹得不可开交，寺院也难免池鱼之殃。村中几位古稀老人听说我是北京来的，拿出很多文件希望我帮着呼吁一下。心中暗自苦笑，但看着他们殷切的表情，又实在不愿打破他们的希望。事实上这件事政府该做的都已经很圆满了，该修的修了，该保护的保护了，该下文件的也下了，文件中提到古寺保护，有"库寺坝三位一体，另成景观"警句，意境深远。剩下具体到村民之间的冲突，还需要互相沟通，多多疏导，但愿神佛保佑，使得人们互相理解，功德无量的寺院早日圆满。
projects.content_en: By the roadside on the way back from Hexi Village (where Sanxian Bridge is) to Chunchi Town, I encountered this old one by chance. Though already in ruins, its character remains. The bridge house's construction is the locally popular style, identical to Sanxian Bridge — one can imagine the original workmanship was also quite intricate. Its frame structure is not the typical woven-timber interlocking frame, but an eight-shaped interlocking: one set of straight transverse timbers, supported below by an eight-shaped frame. The frame structure is clearly visible; though this bridge doesn't look high, incomparable with those great bridges in the mountains, from this angle it still feels a bit dizzying. There is a shrine in the bridge; the frame was once destroyed but remains sturdy, with half left for pedestrians. Its current appearance rather resembles a teaching model for an architecture school — one could consider persuading the president of Tsinghua University to bring this old one back to campus. The setting sun ages, the bridge remains, with Buddhist light still illuminating half. The more I look, the more I feel it was no ordinary thing originally, unexpectedly reduced to this state. I encountered two elders returning from farming; seeing me photographing, they enthusiastically explained the bridge's origins. It is said this bridge is ancient and famous far and wide, originally named "Yuanlin Bridge" — scholars from this township going to take the imperial examination would all come to worship here. Later, due to long neglect, it gradually fell into ruin. In recent years, when a hydropower station was built nearby, this bridge was almost abandoned; because local villagers argued forcefully, the government built a dam upstream, and the bridge was barely preserved. Now everyone wants to repair the bridge, but苦于 no funds. It seems this "Yuanlin Bridge" has extraordinary origins: as the name suggests, it should have been built after someone locally passed the jinshi exam or even became a Hanlin academician, so that later students would come to gain good fortune before exams. As for repair funds, in the past bridge repairs were all through spontaneous fundraising; now the village is full of tall buildings, not looking short of money — it's mainly people's attitudes changing. These two elders, public-spirited and righteous, hearing I was doing ancient architecture research, led me to see a thousand-year-old ancient temple by the bridge, founded over 1,300 years ago — earlier than the Tang. This Prajna Chan Temple was restored in the 1980s, but good things never come easy: first the upstream hydropower station was built, the temple almost flooded; later people from neighboring villages, over fengshui issues, had a huge dispute with the village people, making a terrible scene, and the temple inevitably suffered collateral damage. Several seventy-year-old elders in the village, hearing I was from Beijing, took out many documents hoping I would help advocate. I smiled bitterly to myself, but seeing their earnest expressions, I really didn't want to shatter their hopes. In fact, what the government should do has been done thoroughly: what should be repaired has been repaired, what should be protected has been protected, what documents should be issued have been issued — the documents mention ancient temple protection with the aphorism "reservoir-temple-dam as one, forming another landscape," profound in meaning. What remains, specifically the conflicts between villagers, still requires mutual communication and more mediation. May gods and Buddhas bless, so that people understand each other, and the temple of boundless merit reaches completion soon.

projects.name: 百祥桥
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 宁德屏南县寿山乡白洋村附近棠溪之上
projects.address_en: Over Tangxi Stream near Baiyang Village, Shoushan Township, Pingnan County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
桥村关系
古道线索
屏南廊桥百千万
国家级文保
石铺古道
projects.content_zh: 百祥桥又名白洋桥，顾名思义距离屏南县寿山乡白洋村不远，而手头资料显示其位于棠口乡际头村北1公里处，与实际出入较大。到际头村口打听此村，本以为近在咫尺，哪知村民们说距离非常远，而且路非常难走，小轿车根本开不上去，只有拖拉机可以。要么就是走着看，往返差不多一整天。我有些犹豫，但百祥桥是国家级文物保护单位，咬咬牙还是要上，否则对自己难以解释。当地人很热心，帮我联系了一位向导梁老伯，他在一个大型养猪场附近等我。开始一段车能凑合走，但非常艰难，以至于车速与走着差不多，而且总是担心尖利的石头把车胎硌破了。好在联系梁老伯还算顺利，开始和他一起上车的还有一位当地大侠，二人都很爽朗，而且看上去都是刚喝了。我问他们这一带是不是都是客家人，他们大声答曰"是呀是呀"，问他们客家人的渊源，他们就不知所云了，不过也难为他们。其间大侠问我："老板你是福州人？"我说："不是，我是北京的。"大侠说："电视里你们北京人说话嘴里就像含着一个鸡蛋。"我无言以对，不过他说的有一定道理，如果客家话是大宋官话，那么北京话无疑就是金兀术汉语了。每当感到困难时，身边总是这般风景在鼓励你前进。后来大侠下车了，而剩下大段的路我们也只有步行了。梁老伯60多岁年纪，但普通话说得不错，我们可以比较顺利地交流。他为人很开朗健谈，而且一旦你提个话头，他总是大声地回应"是呀"、"对呀"云云，一点也不会冷场，有点像个小孩儿。也许山里人都是这种开朗的性格，不禁让我想起《约翰·克里斯朵夫》里面描写的乡人的形象，比较亲切。路程比我想象的还要漫长，走山路梁老如履平地，我就难免有些暴露本来面目。他安慰我说你们城里人不习惯，我们乡下人走惯了的。和他谈起附近的廊桥，他也很自豪，说我们屏南的廊桥是"百千万"。百是眼前的百祥桥，千是千乘桥，万是万安桥，形容有趣，而且细想想"百"一个洞，"千"两个洞，"万"八个洞……有点像打麻将。不过"万千"易得，一"百"难求，能知道并到过百祥桥的人怕是很少。要知道途经的小村庄已经基本无人居住了。我问他，您觉得这木拱桥的手艺是本乡本土旧有的还是外面传进来的。他说本乡也有师傅，也有外乡请的……所答非我所想，罢了。闽北的山区有一个好处，就是付出多少辛苦，必然得到多少快乐，越是山路崎岖人烟稀少，景色越是美得出奇，加之前两天刚下过雨，空气有如水洗的一般。渐渐地，脚下出现石铺的古道，梁老说这是以前通往宁德的要道，没有公路的时候很热闹的，现在都废弃了，沿着古道走下去就快到百祥桥了。不过走到最后连梁老都有点"二或"了：我都十几年没有下到这里了，怎么走了这么久一个人都没碰到？
projects.content_en: Baixiang Bridge, also called Baiyang Bridge, as the name suggests is not far from Baiyang Village in Shoushan Township, Pingnan County, while available materials show it is located 1 km north of Jitou Village in Tangkou Township — quite different from reality. Asking about this village at the entrance of Jitou Village, I thought it was close at hand, but villagers said it was very far away and the road was very difficult — small cars simply couldn't drive up, only tractors could. Either walk and see, round trip almost a full day. I hesitated, but Baixiang Bridge is a national-level cultural heritage site, so I gritted my teeth and decided to go up — otherwise I couldn't explain it to myself. Locals were very helpful and helped me contact a guide, Old Liang, who waited for me near a large pig farm. The first stretch the car could勉强 go, but very difficult, so the speed was about the same as walking, and I always worried sharp stones would puncture the tires. Fortunately contacting Old Liang went smoothly; with him in the car was also a local hero, both very hearty and apparently just had a drink. I asked if this area was all Hakka people; they loudly answered "yes yes," but when asked about Hakka origins, they didn't know what to say — though it's hard to blame them. The hero asked me: "Boss, are you from Fuzhou?" I said: "No, I'm from Beijing." The hero said: "On TV, you Beijing people talk like you have an egg in your mouth." I was speechless, but he had a point — if Hakka is the Great Song official language, then Beijing dialect is undoubtedly Jin Wuzhu's Chinese. Whenever feeling difficulty, the scenery around always encourages you forward. Later the hero got off, and for the remaining long stretch we could only walk. Old Liang was in his 60s but spoke Mandarin well, so we could communicate fairly smoothly. He was very outgoing and talkative, and once you brought up a topic, he always loudly responded "yes" "right" and so on, never letting the conversation die down — a bit like a child. Perhaps mountain people all have this cheerful personality, reminding me of the villagers described in "Jean-Christophe," quite亲切. The journey was longer than I imagined; walking mountain roads Old Liang was as if on flat ground, while I inevitably暴露 my true colors. He comforted me saying you city folks aren't used to it, we country folks are used to it. Talking about nearby covered bridges with him, he was also proud, saying our Pingnan covered bridges are "hundred-thousand-ten-thousand." Hundred is Baixiang Bridge before us, thousand is Qiansheng Bridge, ten-thousand is Wan'an Bridge — an interesting description, and thinking carefully: "hundred" has one arch, "thousand" has two arches, "ten-thousand" has eight arches... a bit like playing mahjong. But "thousand and ten-thousand" are easy to get, one "hundred" is hard to求 — few people know of and have visited Baixiang Bridge. You should know the small villages passed through are basically uninhabited now. I asked him, do you think this timber-arch bridge craft is native to this township or introduced from outside? He said there are local masters and also those hired from outside... not answering what I thought, forget it. The mountainous areas of northern Fujian have one advantage: however much hardship you付出, you必然 get that much joy; the more rugged the mountain road and sparse the population, the more extraordinarily beautiful the scenery — plus it had rained two days before, the air was as if washed. Gradually, stone-paved ancient paths appeared underfoot; Old Liang said this was formerly the main route to Ningde, very busy before highways existed, now all abandoned — following the ancient path down, we would soon reach Baixiang Bridge. But by the end even Old Liang was a bit confused: I haven't come down here for over ten years, how come we've walked so long and not met a single person?

projects.name: 广福桥
projects.address: 宁德屏南县岭下乡岭下村
projects.address_en: Lingxia Village, Lingxia Township, Pingnan County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
姊妹桥
桥村关系
古道线索
元统元年始建
五显大帝神龛
projects.content_zh: 广福桥位于屏南县岭下乡岭下村，与广利桥数百米之隔，为比较少见的一对姊妹桥。广福桥初建于元代元统元年，清嘉庆十二年重修。桥长29.3米，宽4.6米，拱跨25.7米，桥面距水面10.5米。广福桥的外观与广利桥相近，廊屋顶部的弧度稍逊，两边四面修有石阶。廊屋内风雨板全封闭，光线较暗，地面拱起，铺以鹅卵石，铺设规整，保存完好。廊屋11间48柱，四柱九檩抬梁式木架构。中间供奉神龛，祀五显大帝。可能因为近代多次重修的缘故，廊屋内未见题跋。桥头立有嘉庆年重修时的石碑。广福桥紧邻村庄，与人们日常生活联系紧密，不但时有祈福祭祀，也是人们平时休息聚会的场所。
projects.content_en: Guangfu Bridge is located in Lingxia Village, Lingxia Township, Pingnan County, separated from Guangli Bridge by only a few hundred meters — a relatively rare pair of sister bridges. Guangfu Bridge was first built in the first year of Yuantong reign (Yuan Dynasty) and restored in the twelfth year of Jiaqing reign (Qing). It is 29.3 meters long, 4.6 meters wide, with an arch span of 25.7 meters, and the deck is 10.5 meters above the water. Guangfu Bridge's appearance is similar to Guangli Bridge, with the curvature of the covered hall roof slightly less, and stone steps built on all four sides. Inside the covered hall, the wind-and-rain boards are fully enclosed, the light is dim, the ground arches upward, paved with cobblestones neatly laid and well-preserved. The covered hall has 11 bays and 48 columns, with a four-column nine-purlin beam-lifting timber frame. In the middle stands a shrine enshrining the Five Manifest Emperors (Wuxian Dadi). Perhaps due to multiple restorations in modern times, no inscriptions are seen inside the covered hall. At the bridgehead stands a stone stele from the Jiaqing-era restoration. Guangfu Bridge is adjacent to the village and closely connected to people's daily lives — not only are there prayers and sacrifices from time to time, but it is also a place for people to rest and gather.

projects.name: 广利桥
projects.address: 宁德屏南县岭下乡岭下村
projects.address_en: Lingxia Village, Lingxia Township, Pingnan County, Ningde
highlights: 木拱桥结构
姊妹桥
桥村关系
古道线索
宋代始建
斗拱雕刻精细
梁檩题记极多
projects.content_zh: 广利桥又名花桥，坐落在屏南县岭下乡岭下村村头路边，是广福桥的姊妹桥。导航到岭下村，无须打听便能看见。广利桥始建于宋代，明正统年间重建，清乾隆三十九（1774年）年再重建。桥长28.3米，宽4.3米，拱跨19.2米，桥面距水面7.3米。桥两侧有石阶，底部架构三节苗9根。桥外观端庄严整，朴实无华，但廊屋顶部做成一定弧度，虽不似"田地桥"那么灵动，工艺上也见功夫。双坡顶，防护板齐全。廊屋11间46柱，四柱九檩抬梁式木架构，衔接处采用斗拱，雕刻精细。风雨板全封闭，光线较暗。地面鹅卵石铺就，保存完整。桥中间供有神龛，祀真武大帝。广利桥内之上梁檩题记极多，且字迹大多清晰，多数是捐赠者姓名和祝福语，另外有敬佛禅语和诗词楹联等，唯独少见修建工匠的信息。有趣的是广利桥、广福桥这对姊妹俱保存完好，是不多见的。也许初建时是两个相邻的村庄，为了锁住风水，相继在村的水尾建桥，或许再有点互相攀比竞争的意思也未可知。现在这一对姊妹双双被定为省级文物保护单位，又双双入选世界文化遗产备选名录"闽东北廊桥"，也算是一段佳话。
projects.content_en: Guangli Bridge, also called Flower Bridge, sits by the roadside at the head of Lingxia Village, Lingxia Township, Pingnan County, and is the sister bridge of Guangfu Bridge. Navigate to Lingxia Village and you can see it without asking. Guangli Bridge was first built in the Song Dynasty, rebuilt during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, and rebuilt again in 1774 (the 39th year of Qianlong reign, Qing). It is 28.3 meters long, 4.3 meters wide, with an arch span of 19.2 meters, and the deck is 7.3 meters above the water. There are stone steps on both sides of the bridge, and the bottom frame has 9 three-section miao timbers. The bridge's appearance is dignified and neat, plain and unadorned, but the top of the covered hall is made with a certain curvature — though not as lively as "Tiandi Bridge," the craftsmanship shows skill. Double-slope roof, with complete protective boards. The covered hall has 11 bays and 46 columns, with a four-column nine-purlin beam-lifting timber frame; the joints use bracket sets (dougong), with fine carving. The wind-and-rain boards are fully enclosed, the light is dim. The ground is paved with cobblestones, preserved intact. In the middle of the bridge stands a shrine enshrining the True Martial Emperor (Zhenwu Dadi). There are extremely many inscriptions on the upper beams and purlins inside Guangli Bridge, and most of the handwriting is clear — mostly donor names and blessings, plus Buddhist Zen sayings and poetry couplets, but rarely information about the construction craftsmen. Interestingly, this pair of sisters, Guangli Bridge and Guangfu Bridge, are both well-preserved, which is rare.
